subject: OPEN statement with OUTPUT phrase (positioning of the output file with regard to physical page boundaries)
notes: §14.9.27.4 GR18 (cite.py OK §14.9.27.4 18)) leaves positioning with respect to physical page boundaries to the implementor; WiseOwl COBOL's answer is 'top of the first physical page, nothing written by the OPEN'. Verified in code: OpenWriter(FileMode.Create) writes nothing; BeginLinagePage (SequentialConnector.cs:497) sets LinageCounter = 1 and _topMarginPending, materialized by EmitTopMarginIfPending before the first presentation; Advance (L1170) writes '\f' for ADVANCING PAGE on a non-LINAGE file. Probes probe/pg.cob --std 2023 (LINAGE-COUNTER after OPEN = 0001; LINAGE file with one WRITE = CRLF CRLF AAA CRLF; LINAGE file with no WRITE = 0 bytes; line-sequential and record-sequential first WRITE AFTER ADVANCING PAGE = \f then the record) and probe/pg85.cob --std 85 (same bytes). The pb523 goldens pin the LINAGE half (page 1 begins at the file's first physical line, top margin on the medium); the non-LINAGE form-feed half has no golden. This row discharges determination D of kb/Work PB322 (open; its other determinations A/B/C/E/F stay open).
